summary: Implemented in full. (1) Maps centre: the Maps nav now opens a catalogue-driven centre backed by GET /v1/decision-maps through a new authenticated proxy route /api/visual/{endpoint_id}/decision-maps (bridge tokens stay server-side, as with every other visual route). Cards group by the generic theme field in the DECISION_MAPS.md order and show title, decision, readiness and freshness (recipe version + validation kind — no timestamp is invented). A ready card runs its declared capability with only the arguments the recipe advertises, clamped to the declared minimum/maximum; a waiting card lists the exact required_inputs whose status is not 'available' and renders no run affordance at all. The centre replaced the old 'open the last figure mentioned in chat' behaviour entirely. (2) Validated-decision-map treatment: when a visual carries view validated-decision-map, 'How this map was tested' renders in the reading flow — immediately under the map in the chat card, and in the panel caption directly after the claim, before chips, limitations and provenance. It is never behind the audit link or a details accordion, and the validation-summary visual is removed from the supporting rail so it cannot also be a click-to-open card. The panel states validation kind, split rule, training/validation periods, sample sizes, every declared check as value-against-threshold with operators in words, pass state as a word plus a mark (checkmark met / cross not met, so greyscale and screen readers carry it), the producer's bounded claim verbatim, and the validation-scoped limitations. (3) Marks: observations withheld for testing share the observed evidence class with the observations used to fit, so colour cannot separate them — the withheld layer is drawn as a crossed ring in both renderers (SVG figure map and the Leaflet panel map, plus a matching legend swatch). A location flagged by the producer's declared selected_field wears a heavy ink collar in both renderers and for both geometries (cells on the hindcast recipe, points on the spatial-holdout recipe), and the legend names it 'chosen within the declared budget (n)'. (4) Fail-closed: selectionAllowed() gates on answer.validation.status === 'passed'; anything else sets suppressSelection, which both map renderers honour, so no place can be styled as selected or recommended without a pass. The failed state keeps every observed and withheld layer, shows the failed checks, and says plainly in the same visual field that no place is marked for action. (5) Layer toggles: one bar driven by the producer's own layer ids and legend labels, working against SVG layer groups and against registered Leaflet overlay objects. Toggling only adds or removes drawn marks — it never recomputes, never changes a producer value, and never hides the validation panel. (6) Nothing dispatches on a subject, place, intervention or recipe id; every label, threshold, evidence class and style role is read from the envelope. Geometries continue to load through immutable result-data handles via the existing authenticated proxy; no GeoJSON is embedded in the catalogue or in chat markdown. A result opened from the Maps centre and the same result opened from chat both go through openInPanel and the same stage code, so layers, validation state, limitations, provenance and the rerun action are identical by construction.
consumer_note: Fixtures are real producer output captured from the live Valparai endpoint, payloads included, so the visual lab renders the whole treatment with no backend running: 12-decision-map-hindcast-passed (mammalia, budget 6 — passed, 6 cells selected), 13-decision-map-hindcast-failed (all taxa — a genuine live failure: AUC 0.477 against a 0.550 threshold, 0 selected cells, other three checks met), 14-decision-map-spatial-holdout (regeneration tree species richness, budget 8 plots — 123 plots across 17 landscapes, 18.6% MAE improvement). The failed case did not need to be hand-authored; the live pack produces it. decision-map-catalog.json captures all seven recipes (2 ready, 5 awaiting-validation-data) for Maps-centre tests. Committing these payloads required an exception to the odysseus .gitignore 'data/' rule — earlier fixture payloads had never been tracked, so a fresh clone could not render the lab; that is now fixed for every fixture. Two notes for the producer: (a) the catalogue carries no per-recipe last-run or generated-at field, so 'freshness' on a card is currently the recipe version plus the validation kind — a producer-supplied last-run timestamp or latest-result pointer would let the centre show real recency without the consumer inventing it; (b) the withheld and fitting observation layers overlap heavily at the roadkill recipe's default extent, so the crossed-ring mark is doing all the separating work at low zoom — a producer-declared render order or an offset hint is not required, but would help. Neither blocks anything.
